clue.text: On top of the moon, called round like man with bottle on 7

definitions.text: On top of the moon, called round like man with bottle on 7

parts.words: On top of the moon, called round like man with bottle on 7
parts.note: a song line for being elated, as over the moon, and also how a drinker with a bottle would be on the American national holiday that 7 names

explanation.surface: Someone over the moon gets a call, like a man drinking on a national holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is from the South Pacific song 'A Wonderful Guy': elated, and also high in the drunken sense for the man with the bottle on 7, Independence Day.
explanation.definitionFit: Being joyfully elated, like a flag raised to full height on the American national holiday, is the sense of the song lyric.

clue.text: See 1
Someone's bright idea for a nail about 2.54 cm (one length)

indicators.note: the nail word goes around the other pieces, as 'about' means surrounding

parts.note: a brad is a thin small-headed nail
an inch is 2.54 centimetres
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A measurement note on a small nail is somebody's clever idea.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet invention or original plan that a person thought up is idiomatically called their creation of the mind.

clue.text: Number of surrounding animals put up by one of four

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting the pieces up means the whole run is read from the bottom

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, a number

indicators.note: the word 'of' goes round the animals, as 'surrounding' says

parts.note: taken as written
deer are animals

explanation.surface: A count of the beasts around is raised by one of a group of four people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' reverses the whole run M + OFDEER, giving FREEDOM. The four are Roosevelt's Four Freedoms of 1941.
explanation.definitionFit: Roosevelt named four essential liberties in 1941, including speech and worship, so liberty is one of four.

clue.text: Piece of paper for erratum

definitions.meaning: a small strip of paper, as a betting or pay chit

explanation.definitionFit: A strip of paper and a small error are both standard senses of the same short noun.

clue.text: 4 in French (mostly in French) before the mines go bust

indicators.note: the French pieces come before the rearranged mines

parts.note: en is French for in

indicators.note: only most of the word is kept, its last three letters dropped

parts.note: the French word for French is francais

indicators.note: when the mines go bust their letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A liberty in French, before the mines collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts FRANCAIS to FRANC; 'go bust' rearranges THE MINES into HISEMENT. 4 is FREEDOM, of which the answer is the grant.
explanation.definitionFit: Granting rights or liberation from bondage is a formal word for liberty given, so it stands for 4, the liberty answer.

clue.text: Dine out on Victorian novel, not all the result of decay when 4 came

indicators.note: dine taken out of its order means its letters are rearranged
only part of the novel's title is used, its tail dropped

parts.note: Pendennis is a Victorian novel by Thackeray

indicators.note: what decay results in is its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Eating out over a Victorian book, partly the product of rot when freedom came.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns DINE into INDE; 'not all' cuts PENDENNIS to PENDEN; 'the result of' rearranges DECAY into CEDAY.
explanation.definitionFit: The Fourth of July marks the American declaration of independence from Britain, the day that liberty arrived.

clue.text: I can't make up my mind about the thing at present, doctor

definitions.text: I can't make up my mind

indicators.note: the doctor goes round the other pieces, as 'about' signals

parts.note: it means the thing
here means present, at hand

explanation.surface: An indecisive person speaks about the matter at hand to a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who keeps hesitating and cannot decide would describe themself this way in the first person.

clue.text: It could be silver for putting in one's pocket

definitions.text: It could be silver for putting in one's pocket

parts.words: It could be silver for putting in one's pocket
parts.note: silver suggests coins to pocket, but it points to the proverb about a cloud's bright edge and to the cloth inside a pocket

explanation.surface: Something that might be silver money for your pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: Every cloud has a silver one in the proverb, and a pocket's inner fabric is the same word.

clue.text: Look thus, if possible

indicators.note: a possible version of the words is another arrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: Look like this, if you can.
explanation.walkthrough: SHUFTI is British slang, from Arabic via soldiers, for a quick look.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick glance is called a shufti in British informal speech, a synonym for a look.

clue.text: Old beer I take abroad?

parts.note: ex means former, old
porter is a dark beer

explanation.surface: A former drink I carry overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: A trader who sends goods to foreign markets could say they take things abroad, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Worcestershire sauce has biblical character

indicators.note: the condiment's name has the character's name within it, across the two words

explanation.surface: A bottle of Worcestershire sauce is said to contain a figure from the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacob's twin brother who sold his birthright is an Old Testament figure.

clue.text: Crab swallowing crushed gold does more than tap

indicators.note: the crab sign takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: Cancer is the zodiac sign of the crab

indicators.note: crushed gold is broken up, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A crab eating powdered gold outdoes a tap dancer.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is read as 'one who does more than tap': a performer in clogs, not merely a tap dancer.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer in wooden shoes stamps out rhythms, going further than a tapper, so it is a playful description.

clue.text: Tea, sweetheart? Keep letter for reporter

indicators.note: the sweetheart word keeps the other piece inside it

parts.note: darling is a term of endearment

indicators.note: a reporter speaks, so the letter is written as it is said

parts.note: the letter G, said as gee

explanation.surface: Tea, dear? Hold a letter for a journalist.
explanation.walkthrough: JEE is how the letter G sounds, spelt out.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine black tea grown in the Indian hill district of that name is a kind of tea.

clue.text: Thingamyjig has intelligence about covers

indicators.note: the intelligence word goes round the covers

parts.note: wit means intelligence, sense
hats are head coverings

explanation.surface: A gadget is clever about its lids.
explanation.definitionFit: A word for an object whose name escapes you, like thingummy, means the same as a thingamyjig.

clue.text: Flowers concealed among killers

indicators.note: the concealed word sits among the killers' letters

parts.note: an orc is a killer whale, or a monstrous killer of fantasy
hid means concealed

explanation.surface: Blooms hidden among murderers.
explanation.definitionFit: Exotic blooms of the family Orchidaceae are flowers.

clue.text: Proverbial aphrodisiac bees can produce

indicators.note: the letters of the two words produce a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Bees can make an aphrodisiac from the proverb.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is 'absence makes the heart grow fonder'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being away is said in the proverb to make the heart grow fonder, so it rouses love.

clue.text: Not too dear a passage in a story

indicators.note: the passage word goes inside the story word

parts.note: a fable is a story
a ford is a place to pass across a river

explanation.surface: A passage in a tale is reasonably priced.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that one can pay for without strain is reasonably priced, not too expensive.

clue.text: Decline to do wrong for money?

parts.note: to sin is to do wrong
K, a thousand, stands for a grand in money

explanation.surface: Would you refuse to do wrong for money?
explanation.definitionFit: To sink is to fall or deteriorate, a synonym for decline as a verb.

clue.text: Girl finds girl embracing girl, right?

indicators.note: one girl's name holds the others inside it

parts.note: Marie is a girl's name
Jo is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl finds one girl hugging another, is that right?
explanation.definitionFit: Marjorie is a female first name, so it stands for a girl.

clue.text: Wagner's in the tower

definitions.meaning: Wagner's four-opera cycle about the Nibelung is known as his cycle by this short name
a set of church bells hanging in a tower is called by this collective name

explanation.surface: Something of Wagner's is up in the tower.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagner's operatic cycle and a full peal of bells in a belfry share the same short name.

clue.text: Burden of wood?

definitions.meaning: to saddle someone with an unwanted load

explanation.surface: Is a weight made of timber?
explanation.definitionFit: Loading someone with an unwelcome task and sawn timber are both senses of the same word.

clue.text: River girl turns to dust

parts.note: the Po is the main river of Italy

indicators.note: the girl's name is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: Nell is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl from the river crumbles to dust.
explanation.definitionFit: The fine powder from flowers is a kind of dust, so the definition is a fair description.

clue.text: Nail broken by unauthorised rules of the church

indicators.note: the nail word is split open by the other piece

parts.note: a claw is an animal's nail
anon, anonymous, here read as un-authored, with no author named

explanation.surface: A nail is broken by unofficial church regulations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unauthorised' is read as 'without an author', giving ANON.
explanation.definitionFit: The body of law governing the Christian church is ecclesiastical law, its rules.
